profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a digital-asset market infrastructure firm between the quantitative research team and the product/market-operations team. The firm is preparing an internal pilot that uses a new CFMM pricing-and-hedging framework to support managed liquidity provision for ETH/USDC pools. The immediate context is a handoff from research to implementation after a paper-style prototype showed promising results on Uniswap v3 and Deribit data. The agenda is to align on what the research package will contain, which pool configuration and market data window the operations team should use, how the daily hedge sheet will be produced, and what counts as the pilot being 'ready' for downstream review. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, dependencies, and next steps for the two workstreams over the next two weeks.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Derivatives pricing, stochastic modeling, and crypto market microstructure
members.background: Former sell-side exotics quant who now leads a small research team building valuation and hedging models for on-chain liquidity products.
members.private_state: Wants the pilot to preserve the mathematical integrity of the new intrinsic-liquidity framework and avoid being judged on a simplified implementation that strips out key assumptions; is also trying to protect his team from last-minute support requests.
hidden_assumptions: A 'hedge-ready' package means a research-grade bundle with formulas, parameter definitions, and a reproducible notebook, not a production-friendly daily file.
The 'ETH/USDC v3 sample pool' refers to the 5 bps pool that the paper's backtest centered on unless someone explicitly names another fee tier.
A 'daily hedge' is computed on end-of-day marks using the latest close and then passed downstream for execution the next trading morning.
Marking the pilot as 'validated' means the model reproduces the paper's option-strip and impermanent-loss decomposition within tolerance, even if no operational dry run has happened.

members.name: Lena Torres
members.expertise: Cross-functional rollout, market-ops workflows, and vendor/data coordination for digital-asset products
members.background: Former prime-brokerage operations manager who now coordinates implementation between quant, engineering, and trading-ops teams for crypto liquidity products.
members.private_state: Needs a clean handoff that can be slotted into existing operational routines quickly, with minimal bespoke interpretation by traders or engineers; is worried about committing support resources without a concrete operating artifact.
hidden_assumptions: A 'hedge-ready' package means a stable position file or dashboard feed that trading operations can use without reading research notebooks.
The 'ETH/USDC v3 sample pool' refers to the flagship operational pool the firm monitors by default, which is the 30 bps pool unless told otherwise.
A 'daily hedge' means an instruction set generated before the U.S. trading day starts, based on the morning snapshot used in other strategy workflows.
Calling the pilot 'validated' means operations has completed at least one end-to-end dry run with live-format files and handoffs, even if some research diagnostics are still provisional.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a hedge-ready package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree that research will hand over a 'hedge-ready package' next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a research deliverable: intrinsic-liquidity formulas, calibrated parameters, and a notebook that computes fair value and delta/vega-style hedge quantities.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means an operational deliverable: a daily-position output or standardized file/feed with fields, naming conventions, and timestamps usable by trading operations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-functional business settings, 'hedge-ready' sounds like a shared maturity label, so both hear it as evidence of alignment and neither expects the other to mean a different artifact format.

misalignment_points.topic: Which ETH/USDC Uniswap v3 pool is the reference pool
misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly mention using 'the ETH/USDC v3 pool' and 'the same sample pool from the analysis.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the ETH/USDC 5 bps Uniswap v3 pool used in the paper-aligned backtest and liquidity-profile examples.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the ETH/USDC 30 bps pool that operations treats as the standard monitored production benchmark.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both pools are common, both are valid ETH/USDC v3 references, and in a coordination meeting participants often omit the fee tier because they assume the canonical pool is obvious.

misalignment_points.topic: When the daily hedge is measured and handed off
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on producing a 'daily hedge sheet' for the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the hedge sheet is generated from prior-day end-of-day marks after the close, with execution expected on the next business morning.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the hedge sheet is generated from the morning snapshot before the U.S. trading session so it can fit the firm's standard daily runbook.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both methods are plausibly called 'daily,' and because the meeting is about coordination rather than model design, each participant treats the timing convention as already standard and not worth unpacking.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss getting the pilot 'validated' before broader review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes validation means the model outputs match the research benchmark: option-strip replication, intrinsic-liquidity scaling, and acceptable error against historical examples.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes validation means the workflow has successfully completed an end-to-end operational rehearsal with the intended file format, timing, and ownership handoffs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Validation is a prestige term used across research and operations with positive connotations, so each side hears a familiar checkpoint while silently applying different pass criteria.
